title: Consume Terraform networking outputs + add networking preflight checks (endpoints + DNS)
author: Benji Okafor
description: This PR wires the installer to consume networking outputs from the alpha Terraform modules (redwood-terraform/modules/redwood-private-vpc) and adds explicit networking preflight checks for DNS + VPC endpoint reachability before we attempt to pull images or bring up control-plane services. Motivation: we’ve repeatedly seen pilot failures where installs get far enough to start pulling/pushing (ECR/S3/Logs) and then fail with non-obvious errors caused by missing endpoints, private DNS not enabled, or resolver misconfiguration (SUP-2197). With this change, the installer can (a) accept a single Terraform outputs JSON blob and translate it into the installer’s networking config, and (b) provide actionable errors up-front when critical endpoints or DNS are not in place. What’s included: 1) New input mode: --networking-terraform-outputs <path> (or networking.terraformOutputsPath in config) which expects the JSON output from `terraform output -json` for the wrapper module. 2) Translation layer that maps Terraform outputs to the installer’s internal NetworkingConfig, with strict validation for required outputs (vpc_id, private_subnet_ids, isolated_subnet_ids, endpoints.* where applicable). 3) Preflight: `redwood-private-installer preflight network` (also invoked automatically as part of `install` unless --skip-preflight-network is set) that checks: DNS resolution for endpoint hostnames (ecr.api, ecr.dkr, logs, sts; s3 is gateway so we validate route/reachability differently), HTTPS connectivity to interface endpoint DNS names from the runner host, and presence of required endpoints when public egress is disabled. 4) Clear error messages with suggested remediations and links back to the Confluence runbook (Private installer networking preflight checks) and Terraform quickstart. Implementation notes: - Endpoint checks use AWS SDK discovery where possible and fall back to deterministic DNS names from service/region; we intentionally avoid making assumptions about customer custom DNS beyond "can resolve and connect". - For locked-down/no-public-egress installs, we now treat STS as required if installer will call AssumeRole (common in enterprise); otherwise it’s flagged as strongly recommended with a warning and a follow-up prompt. - S3 is a gateway endpoint, so reachability is validated by attempting a HEAD request against the regional S3 endpoint and surfacing a specific hint if it fails (missing route to S3 prefix list / no gateway endpoint / blocked by NACL). - This PR does not change defaults in the Terraform modules; it only consumes their outputs and reduces installer ambiguity. Testing: - Unit tests for output parsing/mapping, including partial adoption (existing VPC) cases where certain outputs are absent by design. - Integration test (CI) runs the installer preflight against a sandbox VPC with endpoints enabled; includes a negative test with private DNS disabled to ensure error messaging is actionable. Follow-ups: - PR-389 improves error message formatting and adds doc links for the most common failure modes; kept separate to keep this focused on behavior + contracts.
commits: installer/networking: add Terraform outputs loader + schema validation
preflight: add endpoint DNS resolution + connect checks (ECR/Logs/STS)
preflight: add S3 gateway reachability probe + better hints
tests: fixtures for wrapper module outputs; negative cases for missing endpoints/private DNS
docs: update sample config + add preflight command output examples
conversation: Ethan Park (review): Love the direction. Two asks: (1) make sure installer treats missing STS endpoint as fatal only when we actually need STS (AssumeRole path), otherwise warning; (2) confirm output names match the wrapper module contract in redwood-terraform PR-250 (endpoint IDs vs DNS names).

Benji Okafor (author): Updated logic: STS required iff auth.mode=assume_role OR we detect roleArn configured; otherwise warn. Also aligned output keys to wrapper contract: endpoints.interface.ecr_api_id/ecr_dkr_id/logs_id/sts_id + private_dns_enabled boolean; we derive DNS names at runtime based on service + region and rely on resolver.

Irene Choi (review): For S3, I’m worried an HTTP probe might fail in environments without outbound internet even with gateway endpoint (since it’s still going to the same hostname). How are we ensuring traffic stays inside AWS? Also please avoid suggesting customers "open 0.0.0.0/0" anywhere in hints.

Benji Okafor (author): Good point. The probe uses the regional S3 endpoint hostname but the expectation is that with gateway endpoint, routing to the S3 prefix list stays internal; if customer DNS routes somewhere odd, they’ll fail anyway. I added messaging that focuses on "ensure S3 gateway endpoint + route table association" and removed any hints about broad egress. No 0.0.0.0/0 suggestions.

Victor Alvarez (review): Can we surface which subnets/route tables we think are used for endpoints? In some shared VPCs, endpoints exist but aren’t associated with the right subnets. Even a "check association for subnets: [...]" would help.

Benji Okafor (author): Added context to error output: prints the subnet IDs (private/isolated) from config and says "validate endpoint subnet associations cover these". For gateway S3 we print the route table IDs when present in Terraform outputs; if not present (existing VPC mode), we still point to the configured subnet IDs as the anchor.

Marcus Lin (review): Security: make sure we don’t log sensitive content (account IDs are fine). Also, avoid full URLs with signed headers if we ever add that later. Finally, please ensure we don’t silently pass when private DNS is disabled but endpoints exist; we should fail with a clear remediation for alpha defaults.

Benji Okafor (author): Ack. Logs only include service/region and endpoint IDs (no headers). Private DNS: now hard-fails for required interface endpoints unless user explicitly sets networking.allowPrivateDnsDisabled=true (advanced escape hatch) and even then we emit a big warning + mark configuration unsupported for alpha.
Kira Thompson (review): Please add a short snippet in docs showing how to produce the outputs JSON, and add a sample "good" preflight output so customers know what success looks like.

Benji Okafor (author): Added to docs/preflight.md and docs/configuration.md: `terraform output -json > tf-outputs.json` + example invocation + sample success output. Also linked Confluence runbook for deeper troubleshooting.
Ethan Park (approval): Approved after STS gating + output contract alignment. This should reduce the "ECR pull failed" ambiguity a lot.
Irene Choi (approval): Approved. Thanks for tightening the S3 hints and making private DNS handling explicit.
Marcus Lin (approval): Approved from security perspective with the logging constraints and the alpha guardrail.
release_notes: Installer can now read a Terraform `output -json` file from the Redwood Private VPC modules and auto-populate networking config.
Added `preflight network` checks for DNS and required interface endpoint reachability (ECR/CloudWatch Logs/STS) with actionable remediation hints.
